addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- fluxcd: Flux CD GitOps agent — manages Kubernetes clusters using GitOps principles. Answers Flux questions, generates validated YAML manifests, debugs live clusters via the flux-operator MCP, and audits GitOps repositories. Use when users ask about Flux CD, Flux Operator, GitOps workflows, or Kubernetes deployments managed by Flux.
 (Tools: All tools)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- laravel:laravel-simplifier: Simplifies and refines PHP/Laravel code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- 1password: Set up and use 1Password CLI for sign-in, desktop integration, and reading or injecting secrets.
- adr
- agent-browser: Legacy CDP browser-automation CLI (not installed by default). Use ONLY when Luke explicitly asks for agent-browser or its niche features (Electron app automation, Vercel Sandbox / Bedrock cloud browsers, video recording). All other browser work routes via browser-toolkit (surf default).
- agent-ci: Run GitHub Actions CI locally with Agent CI to validate changes before pushing. Use when testing, running checks, or validating code changes.
- agent-context: Agent context/observation router: memory, handoff, screen history, browser state, transcripts, context usage. Use for prior work or ambiguity.
- agent-native-hardening
- agentic-mapreduce: Whole-repo completeness tasks (invariant sweeps, audits, migrations) via Agentic MapReduce: deterministic selectors → sharded signals → parallel workers → schema'd findings → reduce+verify. Use when the entire codebase must be considered.
- anthropic-tools: Anthropic/Claude API tool + context engineering reference library. Child refs: tool search, programmatic tool calling, tool combinations, web search/fetch, bash, context management, compaction, context editing, cache diagnostics. Use when building/reviewing Claude API agents.
- asset-of-value: Asset of Value (AOV/Aurik/Pavlo Phitidis) framework for transferable, system-led businesses. Use when: AOV, owner/founder dependency, sellable business, succession, exit readiness, valuation levers, key-person risk.
- autoreview: Structured code review closeout via Codex (default) or Claude. Use when: autoreview, Codex review, Claude review, second-model review, after non-trivial edits before commit/ship, or reviewing a local/PR branch after fixes.
- babysit: Pilot all active agent sessions to completion unattended (overnight) across usage-window resets — triage, nudge, course-correct, close out, journal, morning report. Use when Luke says babysit my sessions, going to sleep with sessions running, or /babysit.
- bearings: Orient on a target (project/repo/incident/decision) — ground current state from live evidence, name the desired state, surface the gap, return prioritized next actions. Use when picking up work, context-switching, incident triage, or asked "where are we / status / what next".
- browser-toolkit
- chrome-devtools: Uses Chrome DevTools via MCP for efficient debugging, troubleshooting and browser automation. Use when debugging web pages, automating browser interactions, analyzing performance, or inspecting network requests. This skill does not apply to `--slim` mode (MCP configuration).
- clean-coder: Professional coding discipline inspired by Uncle Bob. Use when user asks for clean-coder, Uncle Bob, professional coding principles, frustration/pressure, no slop, or ship-readiness guardrails.
- cli-tool-fork: Manage Luke's personal/forked CLI tools — fork provenance, verify gate, versioned releases, changelog, and Homebrew tap via valkyriweb/tap. Use when forking a CLI, cutting a release, bumping the tap formula, or syncing from upstream.
- cloud-stacked-diffs: Deliver multi-step work as stacked draft PRs — one branch per step, each targeting the previous step's branch. Use when asked for stacked PRs/diffs, a PR stack/chain, or splitting a large task into dependent PRs for incremental review.
- code-craft
- codebase-improvement-stack: Full codebase improvement stack: /goal execution, Effect for TS/JS, code-craft, Matt Pocock architecture lens, codex review, clawpatch, GitHub/ClawSweeper/Paperclip/Multica coordination, PR cleanup, CI, deploy readiness. Use for quality loops, PR flows, issue triage.
- component-tree-planning: Plan frontend features/refactors with component-tree diagrams before coding. Use when building/refactoring UI, reducing complex state or excess useEffects, planning Storybook-first work, or defining component hierarchy, props, and state ownership.
- computer-use: Use Orca's computer-use CLI to inspect and operate local desktop app windows through accessibility trees, screenshots, and safe UI actions. Use for desktop app interaction: list apps/windows, get app state, read visible UI, click controls, type, press keys, scroll, drag, set values, or perform accessibility actions. Also use for browser windows, webviews, Orca app UI, or other desktop UI. Triggers include "computer use", "orca computer", "read Spotify", "read Slack", "control/click/read in a desktop app", and "get app state".
- context-engineering
- crabbox: Lease remote Linux compute with crabbox. Default = Luke's lue-kube in-cluster HA runner pool (provider: ssh, no device pin); fallback = static-SSH to old-mbp/x99/Mac Mini. Use when the laptop can't run CI-grade, cross-OS, or sandboxed workloads.
- create-cli: CLI UX/spec: args, flags, help, output, errors, config, dry-run.
- deliberate: OODA Orient→Decide: explore current state, turn blockers into decision briefs with pros/cons + recommendation, then name the next action. Use when: deliberate, orient-decide, unblock-brief, autounblock, orient so I can decide, or what's blocking you.
- design-md: Author/review/refine a DESIGN.md — a numeric design-system contract (tokens, type, spacing, motion, components, do/don'ts, decisions log) humans and agents build UI against. Use when creating/refining one or gating UI PRs; not for ADRs or redesigns.
- development
- diagnose
- docs
- domain-dns-ops: Luke's private domain/DNS ops router for ~/Projects/manager: domain inventory, registrar delegation, Cloudflare DNS/routes/redirects, and verification. Use when managing domains, DNS records, nameservers, Cloudflare zones/routes, redirects, or registrar handoffs.
- effect: Effect router for TS/Node: typed errors, Services/Layers, config, retries/timeouts, observability, resource safety, or wrapping Promise boundaries. New app → effect-new-project; existing repo → effect-incremental-adoption; reactive UI state → references/effect-atom.md.
- evals
- feature-flag-development
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- forge: Software-factory / agentic-SDLC doctrine router: loop design, review economy, fitness ratchets. Use when: designing agentic loops/pipelines, cutting token waste in CI reviews, factory work, forge sphere, agent SDLC efficiency.
- fork-maintenance: Maintain a personal fork of an upstream repo (origin = Luke's fork, upstream = original). Use when: sync a fork, pull/cherry-pick upstream changes, install a fork over the npm/pnpm-installed binary, or set up a new fork.
- frontend
- github: GitHub router for `gh` CLI work: issues, PRs, Actions runs, API queries, reviews, author context, queue triage, and cache hygiene. Use for any GitHub task, especially when the user mentions gh, issue, PR, CI/checks, Actions, repo triage, or GitHub API.
- gmail-email-formatting: Format and safely send email reports through Gmail or another email client. Use when composing/sending emails, Gmail messages, email reports, gog gmail send, or when user asks to report via email.
- go
- gog: Google Workspace CLI (gog). Use when accessing Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Contacts, Tasks, Apps Script, or Workspace Admin — or when the user says gog/gws.
- gpt-image-edit-prompts: Prompt patterns for GPT Image 2 image-to-image edits. Use when writing prompts to edit an existing image: identity preservation, embedded text rewriting, background swaps, headline/CTA changes, translated variants.
- grill-to-ship-workflow: Turn fuzzy intent into shipped work: grill-me-with-docs → PRD/spec → issues → /goal → TDD → review → PR/merge/deploy/smoke/rollback. Use when Luke wants robust specs, rapid implementation, issue triage, PR flows, or state-controlled deployment.
- harness-loop: Harness-loop parent. Use for goal runs, durable/thread automations, eval-gated sprints, autonomous workers, PROGRESS.md/PLAN.md orchestration, and quality gates.
- herdr: Control herdr workspaces, tabs, panes, and agent status from inside herdr. Use when HERDR_ENV=1 and you need pane/session orchestration.
- html: Self-contained house-styled HTML artifacts instead of Markdown/chat: diff/PR viewers, dashboards, reports, plans, slide decks, SVG diagrams, editor UIs. Use when: make an HTML, artifact/report/explainer, output meant to be read/compared/interacted with.
- imagegen-frontend-web: Premium frontend image direction. Generate one horizontal image per section; varied composition, CTAs, hero scale, palette, second-read details.
- improve: Read-only senior-advisor survey producing prioritized, self-contained plans — never edits anything. Routes /improve to a codebase audit (this file) or a business/strategy audit (business-playbook child). Use only on explicit /improve.
- infra-deployment
- jellyfin: Operate Luke's Jellyfin: playback/admin CLI, user management, library scans, logs, troubleshooting, and lue-kube Jellyfin checks. Use when user mentions Jellyfin, media server users, Jellyfin playback/control, or Jellyfin problems.
- k8s
- land: Act-lane closeout: run polish proof gates, babysit PR/CI, merge when authorized, canary deployed work, report landing readiness, and work-closeout. Use when: land, babysit to merge, ready to merge, ship/merge this, canary, landing report.
- library: Query the Resource Library (durable OKF domain knowledge) via the `library` CLI — catalog / get <id> / search. Use to recall project/system facts, decisions, or captured references before setting a target or weighing options.
- linear-local-first-architecture: Use when building a web app that must feel instant, when users complain about spinners or perceived slowness despite acceptable latency, or when designing a local-first sync architecture with optimistic updates.
- lore: Search, recall, and manage Luke's archived agent sessions (pi/codex/claude) via the lore CLI. Use when asked to find a past session, recall/restore an old conversation, check session backup or archive health, or run session backups and truncation.
- mac-health: Mac sweep/health triage via Luke's mac-health CLI. Use when: /mac-health, /mac-sweep, Mac lag, CPU/RAM/swap pressure, heat, throttling, fans, battery drain, or resource cleanup.
- macos: macOS router — local upkeep, remote-Mac over SSH, SSH repair, native automation, Peekaboo desktop control. Use for any Mac maintenance/automation/SSH task.
- maintainer-orchestrator: Delegated maintainer ops: decision-ready PRs, worker monitoring, queue cleanup, releases.
- markit: Convert files and URLs to markdown using the markit CLI. Use when the user provides a document, image, audio file, or URL to convert.
- matt-pocock
- mcp-builder: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK).
- model-hierarchy: Pick the right provider+model tier when delegating to a sub-agent or choosing a model manually. Use when: spawning a sub-agent, deciding which model for a task, a model feels like overkill, or balancing quota. NOT a classifier for `auto` aliases (the vLLM SR router handles those). Triggers: "which model", "spawn agent", "model routing", "too heavy for this", "save quota".
- notes: Maintain a running implementation-notes.md decision log while implementing a spec. Use when the user asks for /notes, implementation notes, decision logging, ambiguity tracking, or wants spec interpretations, deviations, tradeoffs, and open questions captured during coding.
- opik: Opik LLM observability router (self-hosted at opik.bermont.digital). Use when: Opik traces, token audit, cost/token drain, datasets, experiments, feedback scores, SkillOS evaluation, remote agent observability.
- oracle
- orchard: Orchard sphere: move a Seeber Group business through its BDLC lifecycle (Seed→Root→Grow→Fruit→Prune/Graft, +Tend) — place its phase, pick phase-correct gated Paperclip actions. Use when: a company/venture/client-line/idea as a business; BDLC.
- pi: Pi router for extension, fork, cache, workflow, runtime, and inter-agent comms work. Use for Pi/my-pi/pi-mono/cache/tools/forkAgent.
- pi-update: Update the local Pi (pi-mono fork): sync from upstream, integrate fork patches, rebuild the coding-agent binary, refresh extensions. Use when updating Pi, pulling upstream into the fork, or rebuilding so the local `pi` CLI picks up code changes.
- pinchtab: Token-efficient browser automation via PinchTab using stable accessibility refs (`e5`, `e12`). Use when a task needs to open sites, click/fill flows, scrape text, export screenshots/PDFs, manage profiles or multiple instances, or fall back to the HTTP API.
- planning
- polish: Quality/proof loop before land: define success criteria, verify with artifacts, run review lenses, track surfaced work, close out. Use when: prove done, quality gate, ship-readiness, final review before land. Diff cleanup -> code-review.
- pr-bots: PR automation router — drive a PR to green, craft/architecture review, docs freshness, closeout stitching. Use for any automated PR review/fix/closeout task.
- progression-os: Luke's Progression OS router — move intention to outcome via loop, currencies, durable state, and earned trust. Use when designing project operating models, confidence gates, autonomy, closeout, or bearings.
- project-init: Bootstrap a new project from zero: confirm name + workspace, create GitHub repo (private, valkyriweb default), git init, AGENTS.md, .gitignore, CI/deploy stubs, Paperclip register, ClawSweeper. Triggers: 'new project', 'scaffold a repo', 'init project'.
- project-sdlc
- qmd: Search markdown knowledge bases, notes, and documentation using QMD. Use when users ask to search notes, find documents, or look up information.
- reporter: Turn raw agent evidence into digestible reports: canonical report with exec summary, TOC, linked evidence, plus WhatsApp/voicenote/graph short forms. Use when asked for a report, proof pack, status digest, or PR/issue evidence summary.
- reviewers: Review/ship router for code diffs, PRs, Hunk sessions, polish, /go, and land handoff. Use for review my code/diff/PR/branch or ship readiness.
- schemator: Use when running Schemator to extract, review, simplify, converge, diff, or report on database schemas, ORM models, migrations, API payloads, JSON Schema, TypeScript interfaces, YAML resources, or other field-based data models.
- schemator-final-report: Use only when preparing, publishing, or reviewing a final Schemator run report; ensures raw artifacts, schema JSON, source details, decisions, verification, and push links are included.
- skill-craft: Skill & agent meta router — author/optimize/clean skills, build agents, curate cross-harness. Use for any work ON skills or agents themselves.
- slop-scan: Run slop-scan as an advisory AI-slop/code-quality heuristic for JS/TS repos. Use when shipping/reviewing JS/TS changes, checking vibe-coded code, or comparing slop deltas before PR.
- social-content-loop: Closed-loop social media agent workflow: plan content, create/revise assets, update canonical schedule state, verify, judge outcome, and continue. Use when any agent plans, creates, approves, schedules, posts, or reconciles social media content.
- stop-slop: Remove AI tells from prose — READMEs, docs, PR/issue text, marketing copy, essays. Use when drafting, editing, or reviewing writing to cut predictable AI patterns.
- storm: Run a STORM-style multi-perspective inquiry: practitioner, skeptic, economist, historian, academic, then synthesize. Use when user says /STORM, STORM, multi-perspective research, or asks to stress-test a topic.
- supabase-postgres-best-practices: Postgres performance optimization and best practices from Supabase. Use this skill when writing, reviewing, or optimizing Postgres queries, schema designs, or database configurations.
- systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- testing
- trackers: Issue-tracking router — Multica (engineering issues, workspaces, projects, agent daemon, execution runs) + Paperclip (control plane: issues, approvals, comments, agents, dashboard, onboard/run/doctor). Use for any Multica or Paperclip work.
- triage: Luke-specific triage router for Paperclip/business admin, email/WhatsApp, GitHub queues, and blocker blitzes. Use when sorting blockers, unblocking Luke, or deciding what needs human input. Not for active outages or code debugging.
- utilities
- webapp-testing: Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.
- weekly-review: Run Luke's weekly review — tools/skills drift audit, project index freshness check, pi cache hit-rate review. Triggers on /weekly-review (slash) or the Monday 9am pi-routine fire.
- wordpress-update: Production WordPress/Woo updates: core, plugins, WP bump, pending updates, live-store safety, SpinupWP, Cloudflare, WP Rocket, Smilerite.
- work-closeout: Session-end closeout: classify dirty files, stashes, WIP branches into six buckets; preserve non-trivial WIP as pushed branch + issue/draft PR + next action. Use when a session ends with dirty repos, WIP handoff, 'closeout', or 'dirty triage'.
- acceptpr: /acceptpr
- create-cli-skill: /create-cli-skill
- fixissue: /fixissue
- landpr: Land PR end-to-end (temp rebase, full gate, merge, thanks).
- merge: Analyze git changes, manage PRs, and safely merge branches
- pickup: /pickup
- refactor: Deep refactoring analysis with cost/benefit guidance
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- codex:rescue: Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent
- codex:setup: Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate
- visual-explainer:diff-review: Generate a visual HTML diff review — before/after architecture comparison with code review analysis
- visual-explainer:fact-check: Verify the factual accuracy of a document against the actual codebase, correct inaccuracies in place
- visual-explainer:generate-slides: Generate a stunning magazine-quality slide deck as a self-contained HTML page
- visual-explainer:generate-visual-plan: Generate a visual HTML implementation plan — detailed feature specification with state machines, code snippets, and edge cases
- visual-explainer:generate-web-diagram: Generate a beautiful standalone HTML diagram and open it in the browser
- visual-explainer:plan-review: Generate a visual HTML plan review — current codebase state vs. proposed implementation plan
- visual-explainer:project-recap: Generate a visual HTML project recap — rebuild mental model of a project's current state, recent decisions, and cognitive debt hotspots
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- codex:codex-cli-runtime: Internal helper contract for calling the codex-companion runtime from Claude Code
- codex:codex-result-handling: Internal guidance for presenting Codex helper output back to the user
- codex:gpt-5-4-prompting: Internal guidance for composing Codex and GPT-5.4 prompts for coding, review, diagnosis, and research tasks inside the Codex Claude Code plugin
- skill-creator:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- visual-explainer:visual-explainer: Generate beautiful, self-contained HTML pages that visually explain systems, code changes, plans, and data. Use when the user asks for a diagram, architecture overview, diff review, plan review, project recap, comparison table, or any visual explanation of technical concepts. Also use proactively when you are about to render a complex ASCII table (4+ rows or 3+ columns) — present it as a styled HTML page instead.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize new CLAUDE.md file(s) and optional skills/hooks with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
